report.summary: Chunk 2 of 7: defines regex patterns for dotted references and path-symbol combinations, dataclasses Reference and DocRefReport, and helper function reference_key.
risks: _DOTTED | medium | Pattern requires first segment lower-case-ish but allows underscores; may miss valid module paths starting with underscore. | Check if modules like '_internal' are expected to be matched.
_PATH_SYMBOL | medium | Pattern requires '.py' extension; may miss references to packages (directories) or other languages. | Verify if only .py files are intended.
_PATH_ONLY | medium | Pattern allows only .py files; similar limitation.
NON_MODULE_DOTTED_NAMES | medium | Hardcoded list may grow stale; new false positives will cause spurious reports. | Ensure regular review or automated detection.
reference_key | low | Excludes line number; may merge distinct references if same raw text on different lines in same doc. | Acceptable trade-off for stability across edits.

handoff.purpose: Define regex patterns for identifying dotted references and path-symbol references, and dataclasses for representing and reporting document references.

symbols.name: _DOTTED
symbols.note: Regex for dotted references with at least two segments, first segment lower-case-ish.

symbols.name: _MODULE_DUNDERS
symbols.note: Frozenset of dunder attributes every module has at runtime.

symbols.name: _FILE_EXTENSIONS
symbols.note: Frozenset of file extensions that indicate a filename, not an attribute.

symbols.name: _NON_MODULE_DOTTED_NAMES
symbols.note: Frozenset of dotted names known not to be module-symbol references.

symbols.name: Reference
symbols.note: Dataclass representing one documentation reference to code.

symbols.name: reference_key
symbols.note: Returns identity key for a reference across edits, excluding line number.

symbols.name: DocRefReport
symbols.note: Dataclass representing measurement results: resolving, broken, skipped references.

claims.text: A dotted reference: at least two segments, first segment lower-case-ish so `Path.resolve` and prose like `Foo.bar` do not enter as module paths.
claims.why: The regex _DOTTED matches strings starting with lowercase or underscore, then a dot, then uppercase/lowercase/underscore segments, ensuring first segment is lower-case-ish.

claims.text: `path/to/mod.py::symbol` and `path/to/mod.py:symbol`. The colon form requires an IDENTIFIER after it, so `daedalus/cli.py:794` (a line number) is not read as a symbol that is missing.
claims.why: The regex _PATH_SYMBOL requires an identifier after the colon/double-colon, so line numbers (digits) are not matched.

claims.text: A bare in-repo module path, no symbol.
claims.why: The regex _PATH_ONLY matches strings ending with .py and no symbol part.

claims.text: Attributes every module has at runtime that no source line declares. Asking ast whether `daedalus` defines `__file__` gets the answer 'no', which is true of the SOURCE and false of the module. Measured: `daedalus.__file__` in docs/adrs/015 was reported broken by the first version of this file.
claims.why: The frozenset _MODULE_DUNDERS contains __file__ and other dunder attributes that are present at runtime but not in source.

claims.text: A dotted reference whose last segment is one of these is a FILENAME, not an attribute. Measured: `room.md` and `parse.rs` were both reported as missing attributes of runs/council/room.py and daedalus/structcore/parse.py.
claims.why: The frozenset _FILE_EXTENSIONS contains common file extensions including 'md' and 'rs'.

claims.text: Dotted inline-code spans that are demonstrably NOT module-symbol references. These are measured corpus ambiguities, not a general vocabulary blacklist: * `core.autocrlf` is Git's configuration key. A coincidental `core.py` made the suffix resolver reinterpret accurate historical prose as a missing Python attribute. * `status.code` is an `OperationStatus` instance attribute. A coincidental `status.py` made the same mistake. The scanner dispatches autonomous edits, so a known false positive must be skipped explicitly rather than left to a writer to 'improve' into falsehood.
claims.why: The frozenset _NON_MODULE_DOTTED_NAMES contains 'core.autocrlf' and 'status.code' as documented.

claims.text: One documentation reference to code, and what became of it.
claims.why: The docstring of Reference class describes it as representing one documentation reference.

claims.text: The identity of a reference ACROSS an edit. Deliberately excludes the line number: correcting a sentence above moves every reference below it, and a key that moved with them would report the original finding as 'withdrawn' for every unrelated edit in the file.
claims.why: The function reference_key returns a string combining doc_path and raw, excluding line number, as described.

claims.text: The measurement: what resolves, what does not, and what was not checked. ``resolving`` is not decoration. It is the denominator that makes the ``broken`` count un-gameable -- see the module docstring.
claims.why: The claim refers to the module docstring which is not present in this chunk.

observations.what: Regex patterns are defined as module-level constants, used for parsing document references.
Frozensets for dunders, file extensions, and non-module dotted names are defined as constants.
Reference dataclass has a to_dict method for serialization.
reference_key function creates a stable identifier across edits by excluding line number.
DocRefReport dataclass provides properties and methods for querying broken and resolving counts per document, and a to_dict method.
